Since, all the bail applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellants i.e. (I.A. No. 01/2022 in Cr.A. No. 1518/2022, I.A. No. 01/2022 in Cr.A. No. 1545/2022, I.A. No. 01/2022 in Cr.A. No.
1866/2022 & I.A. No. 01/2023 in Cr.A. No. 998/2023) arise out of same Special Criminal Case (POCSO Act) No. 13/2019, therefore, they are being decided by this common order.

By the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 08/08/2022, the learned Additional Sessions Judge Gharghoda, District Raigarh (C.G.) in Special Criminal Case (POCSO Act)
No. 13/2019 has convicted and sentenced the appellants as under:-
Conviction Sentence Under Section 457/34 of the RI for 5 years and to pay fine of Indian Penal Code Rs. 500/-, in default of payment to further undergo RI for 1 month.
Under Section 506-II of the RI for 3 years and to pay fine of Indian Penal Code Rs. 500/-, in default of payment to further undergo RI for 1 month.
Under Section 6 of the Life imprisonment (meaning Protection of Children from thereby imprisonment for Sexual Offences Act, 2012 remaining life time of accused/appellants) and to pay fine of Rs. 1000/-, in default of payment to further undergo RI for 2 months.
Mr. Rohitashva Singh, Counsel appears on behalf of appellant Nutan Rathiya in Cr.A. No.
1518/2022.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge Gharghoda, District Raigarh (C.G.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Mr. Aman Kesharwani, Counsel appears for appellant Sugan Singh Rathiya in Cr.A. No.
1545/2022 & for appellants Gocharan Rathiya and Sanjay Rathiya Cr.A. No. 998/2023.

Mr.
Ashutosh Mishra, Counsel appears on behalf of appellant Madhav Rathiya in Cr.A. No. 1866/2022.

It has been argued by the counsel for the appellants that though there are five accused persons involved in the present case, but it was only the case of theft which later on has been coloured in the name of Gang Rape.

It has been further argued that the incident occurred on 17/04/2019 and the police personnel immediately reached to the place of occurrence, but the FIR has been lodged after a long delay of 24 hours of the incident which apparently shows the present case to be a concocted one.

Mr. Rohitashva Singh, Counsel appears on behalf of appellant Nutan Rathiya and Mr. Ashutosh Mishra, Counsel appears on behalf of appellant Madhav Rathiya, further argues that so far as the allegations against appellants Nutan Rathiya and Madhav Rathiya is concerned, they were only standing outside the gate and it is the other three co-accused persons who have entered into the house and committed rape with the two victims who are minor.

They tried to demonstrate the evidence of formal witnesses that the police, just to create the series of offence, came to the spot and registered the case for the offence punishable under Sections 457/34, 376-D, 506- II of the IPC and Sections 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It has been submitted that looking to the allegations against appellants Nutan Rathiya and Madhav Rathiya who are in jail Sugan Sai Rathiya vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101071267/
2 since 19/04/2019, they may be released on bail.
It has been argued for appellants Madhav Rathiya, Gocharan Rathiya and Sanjay Rathiya that there appears to be contradictions in the statements of the two prosecutrix/victim, which goes to show that the participation of these three accused/appellants who are said to committed the rape, is false one.
Ms. Madhunisha Singh, Dy. Advocate General opposes the submission made by the counsel for the appellants and submits that one of the victim who was gang raped by the appellants was minor girl aged about 13 years and injuries on her private part was found.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even the FSL report also found positive.
She further submits that all the three appellants who committed gang rape on the victim were also medically examined and medical examination's report also shows that they have committed the rape.

So far as the elder sister of the victim on whom the rape was committed is concerned, she tried to ran away from the place of occurrence, but the other appellants who were standing outside tried to catch her, but she any how escaped from there
, so the participation of these two appellants also goes to show that they have actively participated with the other three accused persons.
She prays to reject the bail applications.
We have heard learned counsel for the appellants as well as the the State counsel and perused the records of the Court below.

Considering the material available on record, particularly considering the statement of the Victim/Prosecutrix who is minor, the injuries of the victim girl and the FSL report which confirms the happening of rape, we deem it appropriate to reject the applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Accordingly, I.A. No. 01/2022 in Cr.A. No. 1518/2022, I.A. No. 01/2022 in Cr.A. No. 1545/2022, I.A.
No. 01/2022 in Cr.A. No. 1866/2022 & I.A. No. 01/2023 in Cr.A. No. 998/2023 are rejected.
It transpires from the record that the matters are ripe for final hearing.
Let the matters be listed for final hearing.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal (Ramesh Sinha)
